key_insight: Pantagruel trains modality-specific encoders to predict contextualized target representations in a shared feature space rather than modality-tailored tokens or discrete speech units, enabling better capture of both linguistic and acoustic regularities for French text and speech.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between text and speech self-supervised learning for French by replacing modality-specific prediction targets with unified feature-space targets, improving representation quality and cross-modal compatibility.
method: Learn contextualized target representations in a continuous feature space instead of predicting textual tokens or discrete speech units.
Train separate modality-specific encoders (text and speech) to predict those contextualized feature targets so each encoder captures modality-appropriate signals while aligning representations.
Pre-train on large-scale French corpora (e.g., Wikipedia, OSCAR, CroissantLLM and large speech collections) to build strong French-language encoders.
impact: Provides practitioners with stronger, unified French encoders that simplify downstream pipelines (NLP, ASR, speech-text tasks) and improve cross-modal transfer, reducing the need for modality-specific engineering.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: two encoders (text, speech) feeding into a shared feature-space target bank with arrows showing prediction direction.
Before vs After: side-by-side comparison showing token/unit targets vs contextualized feature targets and improved representation overlap.

paper_title: Pantagruel: Unified Self-Supervised Encoders for French Text and Speech
paper_authors: Phuong-Hang Le, Valentin Pelloin, Arnault Chatelain, Maryem Bouziane, Mohammed Ghennai
